item.title: Hybrid diamond chip strengthens interactions between light and quantum bits
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Researchers have developed and demonstrated a new hybrid photonic platform that integrates quantum emitters with photonic devices, providing a way to reliably control the interaction between photons and quantum information carriers. The chip-based platform, which combines gallium phosphide (GaP) with a diamond substrate, could help make quantum networks more practical by providing a way to connect quantum devices over long distances.

item.title: Quantum magic state cleanup cuts errors 40-fold in first successful hardware test
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Qubits, the quantum equivalent of digital bits, are fragile and prone to errors. That makes building reliable quantum computers extremely difficult. One fix has been to use traditional magic state distillation, which filters out flaws, but it is extremely resource-intensive.

item.title: Correcting AI-generated false criminal allegations: a human-rights framework for remedial closure
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hanane Merzougui, Xianghe Gong, Yaohui Liu
Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can fabricate criminal allegations about identifiable people, but the legal difficulty is not confined to correcting the visible output. A false claim may persist in service-side memory, retrieval systems, application programming interface transmissions, risk fields and downstream institutional decisions. Existing scholarship on data rectification, AI supply chains, algorithmic contestability and model correction addresses parts of this problem but does not provide a unified legal test for when distributed remediation is complete. This article develops a propagation-aware standard of remedial closure: a structured test for determining when corrective action has been completed across relevant stages of an AI system.
